shared_elements: upright stone slab as carrying surface
horizontal dividing line or band separating registers
outline arch/dome enclosing the main motif
series of short parallel strokes/verticals along a band
justification: Both are upright, roughly rectangular carved stone panels organised into horizontal registers, and each includes a row of repeated arch/semicircle forms plus a band of short parallel strokes, though in A the arcade sits at the bottom and in B at the top. The decisive difference is manner and content: A is a purely linear, shallow-incised abstract/geometric design with an enclosing dome outline, while B is a deep, modelled relief populated by recognisable animals and figures, so the resemblance stays at the level of generic slab-and-register conventions.
